recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for more explicit CapabilityStatement signaling for system-level conditional delete should be handled as a separate focused tracker, not as remaining FHIR-26646 application work.
issue_request: FHIR-26646 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I R5 change request to define system-level conditional delete, analogous to system-level query, with deleting resources by cross-resource tag as the motivating use case.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 45aaf5e3a78aa816988cc5660e1ea41c6e43673c, which updated source/http.html to add the whole-system conditional delete entry and the `DELETE [base]?[search parameters]` form.
additional_context: source/http.html is in the current build through publish.ini. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-03-30 confirm the work-group decision to update the spec. Later HTTP changes, including FHIR-42728 and FHIR-40772, adjusted conditional interaction names and If-Match handling while preserving the system-level conditional delete endpoint.
reconciliation: No source change was made because current source/http.html already lists whole-system conditional delete, defines both type-level and system-level DELETE search forms, and includes system-path summary rows for conditional delete single and multiple.

related_jiras.note: Later HTTP interaction-code work split conditional interactions into explicit single/multiple names and preserved the system-level conditional delete path in the summary table.
Later HTTP-page work added If-Match handling to conditional delete but did not change the system-level endpoint requested by FHIR-26646.
